title: fleet_burn semantic check: int() truncation before <0 bypasses negative floats in (-1,0)
description: 3x codereview on ozit fix — all 3 passes converged (correctness/security/edge finding 1): scripts/fleet_burn.py:30-32 coerces with int() before the <0 test, so a fractional negative in (-1,0) truncates to 0 and passes as valid -> immediate spurious evaluation/false alarm; bools and numeric strings also coerce silently. Fix: validate the RAW JSON value before coercing; tolerate integral floats (old fleet-driver.sh wrote float usage/ts) but reject bools, non-numeric shapes, and raw negative values. Add a float-shape test.
close_reason: Fixed: fleet_burn.py now validates the RAW JSON value before coercion (_coerce_count): bools, non-numeric shapes (str/list/dict/None), raw negatives including fractional (-1,0) that int() truncated to 0, and non-integral floats are all rejected as corrupt (baseline re-established); integral floats tolerated for legacy snapshots. 3 new hand-oracle tests: fractional negative -0.5 rejected, bool/'100'/100.5 rejected, integral float 100.0 tolerated mid-window. 15/15 pass. One test-oracle error during development (my own expectation miscomputed the window age) was fixed in the test, not the module.
